authors.name: Soumya Susan
authors.bio: A freelance photographer in Hyderabad who began as her church's volunteer photographer. She photographs weddings, portraits and babies, and spends time with children living on the city's streets.

authors.name: Rev. Peggy I. Kennedy
authors.bio: Speaker and author with Two Silver Trumpets Ministry in Canada, where she and Jack Kennedy have served the church for over fifty years.

articles.title: I tried to run away rather than take the photographs, and prayed for ten good shots
articles.deck: Soumya Susan was handed a camera at a children's Christmas drama in 2007 and nearly handed it back. Six years later she is a freelance photographer who thinks of herself as a missionary with a lens.

archiveMeta.editNote: Published as it appeared in the May 2013 issue. Column reading order repaired and typographical errors corrected; the wording is otherwise the author's.

body.v: December of 2007. As New Life Assembly of God Church's official photographer, my first assignment was to capture the Children's Christmas Drama. All that I knew then was to set my frame and click, standing among the crowd. I was in a situation where I had to put my weakness, shyness and fear in a box and shut it for a while in order to click — or alternatively hand over the camera to someone and run away.

I tried running away and refused to click. But I was reminded of the commitment I had made as a volunteer to the media team. I thought about it and prayed: Lord, help me to stand in this huge congregation and still be able to click without my hands trembling. Help me, Lord, get at least ten good shots, so that the Media Director won't get mad at me for trusting me with this job.

And the drama began, and even before I realised, it ended. I let my Media Director take a look at the pictures I clicked. He was kind enough and helped me understand how I could click better. And he told me:
Don't you ever back out before giving something a try.
That was my lesson number one to be a better photographer. And lesson number two: “Don't miss the moment — if it's gone, you can never get it back.”
My act of worship

I now truly believe that this was God's big master plan to use me, a total amateur, to click for His Kingdom. Every time I held the camera, this was my prayer: Lord, help me hold this camera right and never to drop it down. Help me hit the shutter button at the right time. Holy Spirit, I don't know what to click — please take charge of my eyes and vision and capture God's moment happening in His house of worship. I can't sing and worship as I need to click; this is my act of worship. Please accept it. Amen.

This is how the Lord taught me during every event in His house, and took me to new levels. Within no time, I knew the camera settings on my fingertips and managed shoots without being nervous and shy. Soon the church upgraded its photography equipment and I just saddled in with the handling of it. I was really encouraged, and soon our church released the 25th Anniversary Souvenir which had my pictures in it.
I now realised that I was using my talent and gifting to document all that God was doing in church and blessing His people.
My community is my generation

By involving myself in the church media department, I planned to do my B.A. in Mass Communication. I saw how effective visual communication affected my life, and this is what I wanted to do. I wanted God to use me to reach out to my generation through visual media.

My community is my generation. My friends that I hang around with in college, the wonderful people that end up making the pictures I click “picture perfect.” They ask me about my photography story and I tell them that it all started in the house of God. The church where I first knelt down and asked my God to take hold of my life is the same God who has given me a new career lead.

He has not forsaken me and has set me up on higher ground. The work I do makes me depend on Him for creativity, and when I submit to Him and trust in Him, like always, I end up getting beautiful pictures that make me super happy. The events, weddings and portraits I click always have my Father's touch of creativity, because I ask Him to help me — and people do appreciate the pictures. I myself can see the difference: when I do it in my strength I get pressurised, but when Jesus helps me, it's a happy story.
Weddings

I stepped into wedding photography because people told me they liked the pictures, and according to them I clicked much better than the professionals they invested in. And wedding pictures are what families hold dear to their heart. It's once in a lifetime, and I decided that I would want to help them have a beautiful memory of their wedding day. This is my calling — help them preserve their love, because after a few years the pictures I clicked will bring back a smile.

This is what I do today. I freeze precious moments for people and all that they love. Today I cover weddings, birthdays, capture portraits, do baby photography, and enjoy every moment of my dream, believing that one day in God's time I will be a renowned photographer for my Lord and saviour Jesus Christ.
The children on the streets

I have seen myself grow in these six years, from the first time I held the camera till date, and it was all the move of God in my life. I never dreamt of being a photographer — at one time I wanted to be a missionary.

Apart from being passionate about photography, I love to minister to the less privileged children who are homeless and have made their homes on the streets of Hyderabad. I spend time clicking their pictures and playing with them just to love them. One fine day they will know the God who loves the world, as He makes me love them.
Today I'm a freelance photographer depending on Jesus for my career, but I look at myself as a missionary photographer who ministers to kids of my city streets.

Photography was a tiny dot in my life six years ago, but now it's becoming a huge picture in the hands of Jesus — pixel by pixel, every year. This talent which He put in my life is helping me reach out to the world outside my church, and I am enjoying it every bit. Jesus has blessed me to be a blessing, and that is what I will choose to be.

articles.title: Jael's name means “wild goat”, and that is not the insult it sounds like
articles.deck: Rev. Peggy Kennedy on Judges 4 and 5, on a woman who had pitched that tent a hundred times before she used the hammer for anything else, and on what the Hebrew actually means.

archiveMeta.editNote: Published as it appeared in the May 2013 issue. Column reading order repaired and typographical errors corrected; the wording is otherwise the author's.

body.v: The Lord is positioning His people into places of influence and anointing them for service in the sphere of their own influence. This is sometimes in contrast to traditionally held views of the role of believers, as well as the tasks for which the Lord releases His anointing upon His people.
This shift — for purposes of taking the victory of the Lord beyond the usual “fields of engagement”, that is, within the church context — is vividly pictured in Judges 4 and 5.

The prophetic ministry and leadership role of Judge Deborah has prevailed for twenty years in the face of severe oppression and domination of the enemy. The anointing functioned on behalf of domestic needs among God's people. However, it is not until the surprise prophetic announcement in Judges 4:6 that the voice of the anointing addresses the presence of the enemy and the Lord's intended triumph.
The stage is set for great transition

Deborah and Barak come to the mutual understanding that they will commit to partnership, and thus they break the norm for victory to be attained by a single hero. It is important to note that this is not a decision of weakness — Barak is named in the Hebrews 11 line-up of faith. Everything is now in place for not only Barak to be involved with the anointing in a role of military victory, but also opens the way for Jael.
She was not a novice at the swing of the hammer

The story of Jael is well known. She has the famed enemy, Sisera, arrive at her tent door. She comforts him with a refreshing drink. Then she raises her hammer and drives the tent peg through the unsuspecting head of the sleeping enemy.

This is not “conventional” warfare. She represents the new and the now plan of God: to take the battle outside of the four walls of the church, and to use her well-honed skills to defeat the enemy in the sphere of her own influence.

She was not a novice at the swing of the hammer. Likely, every time that tent had moved through the years, she had been the one to raise it and drive the tent pegs to secure it. Now, that same well-honed skill is activated for the purposes of defeating the enemy, and thus advancing the prospering of the people of God both financially and militarily.
The leadership secret is in her name
The “leadership secret” awaits our discovery in the meaning of Jael's name. Granted, it is quite a combination of seemingly unrelated diverse meanings.
We're comfortable and blessed when we realise that firstly “Jael” means valued. That's exactly how the Lord is assessing the role and activity of His people in the marketplace today.

The second meaning is more difficult to appreciate. It means “wild goat”. However, before dismissing this as almost an insult, please note that the original intention of the Hebrew word is all about climbing. Her hammer is activated, and her feet are perfectly formed to ascend.
You are anointed to be sure-footed and to climb.

The Lord values you, and He has outfitted you — even anointed you — to climb the very surfaces of the mountains of society that have previously repelled believers. You won't be pushed back. He's activating your skills and outfitting your feet. He has placed you in the specific sphere of your own influence.
